lede: The longest allocation table in the game — twelve entries, and the nebula lists carry almost all of the weight. The Slugs here do not open a fight by shooting; they open it by switching one of your systems off first, and then shooting. One beacon is placed every single time, and it is the only way into a ship unlock.
callout: **Versus a plain Slug Controlled Nebula:** every other entry is identical — same lists, same minimums, same maximums, same rarity table, same start beacon. The only difference in the whole table is the guaranteed `NEBULA_SLUG_FIGHT_UNLOCK` beacon, which is why this sector is worth routing to and the other one is not.

section_notes.NEBULA_SLUG_FIGHT_UNLOCK: Placed exactly once, and it is a fight from the moment you arrive — the ambusher is invisible to your sensors until it fires. Everything downstream of it hangs on the ship offering to surrender, because the quest marker only exists inside that offer.
section_notes.HOSTILE_SLUG: The non-nebula half of the split, and the small half: one to two beacons here against the nebula list's five to seven. These are ordinary Slug, Mantis, pirate and Rebel ships that shoot straight, plus {{DONOR_BLACK_RAVEN}}, who wants to introduce himself first.
section_notes.NEBULA_HOSTILE_SLUG: The sector's signature, and its biggest single entry. Three of its six events are the remote-hacker family — your doors, your oxygen or your medbay is already dead when the fight starts — and a fourth variant, {{NEBULA_SLUG_CHOOSE_DEATH}}, waits in the neutral list and lets the Slug ask which system you would miss least. A Hacking system counters all four.
section_notes.NEBULA_NEUTRAL_SLUG: The deepest pool in the sector and the least predictable. It holds both of the sector's non-unlock quest starts — {{QUEST_SLUG_PIRATE_TRAP}} and {{NEBULA_BATTLEFIELD}} — alongside {{NEBULA_SLUG_FAKE_STORE}} and {{NEBULA_SLUG_HULLFIX}}, which are a shop and a repair yard right up until they are not.
section_notes.STORM_SLUG: The ion-storm entry, and the one part of the table with no non-nebula twin. The storm suppresses your systems and leaves the Slug ships largely unaffected, so {{STORM_SLUG_FIGHT}} and {{STORM_REBEL}} start with you down a reactor while they are not. {{STORM_BOARDING}} skips the ship fight and sends the boarders straight over.
section_notes.DISTRESS_BEACON_SLUG: The best odds of picking up a Slug crew member in the game sit here, in {{SLUG_DISTRESS_RESCUE}} and {{SLUG_DISTRESS_QUESTION}}. The same list also holds {{SLUG_DISTRESS_TRICK}}, which is a distress call that exists only to get your crew aboard their ship.

chain.title: Slug ship unlock · the construction platform

steps.title: {{NEBULA_SLUG_FIGHT_UNLOCK}}
steps.detail: The guaranteed beacon. Beat the ship down until it offers surrender, then let them live — and when they offer you the prototype weapon, refuse it and ask where it was going instead. Taking the **Anti-Bio Beam** ends the event there; the coordinates are the chain.

steps.title: The platform is already sinking into the clouds
steps.detail: Charging in gets you a fight with the assault ship escort and a good pile of scrap, but the platform is gone. Tailing them quietly is the only branch that continues.

steps.title: Following something you cannot see
steps.detail: Flying toward their last position gets you intercepted; waiting loses them. **Slug crew** reads their life signs through the clouds, and **Sensors 2** overclocks through it — either one waits out the escort until only an interceptor is left.

steps.title: Kill the interceptor before it jumps
steps.detail: A weak ship on a timer — the cruiser is linked to its FTL, so if it escapes the prize goes with it. Destroy it and you get a high standard reward, the **Slug Repair Gel** augment, and the ship unlock.

items.text: The single best system to fly in with. It cancels the remote hack in {{NEBULA_SLUG_DOORS}}, {{NEBULA_SLUG_OXYGEN}}, {{NEBULA_SLUG_MEDBAY}} and {{NEBULA_SLUG_CHOOSE_DEATH}} — four fights that otherwise open with a system already at zero — and sweetens {{NEBULA_AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}} and {{PIRATE_SALESMAN}} on top.

A telepathic duel that can end {{DONOR_BLACK_RAVEN}} without a shot, the ambush spotted early in {{NEBULA_SLUG_FAKE_STORE}}, the dying survivor located in {{NEBULA_BATTLEFIELD}}, an Engi out of {{DONOR_PONY}} with no dice roll attached — and the quiet route through the unlock chain.

Level 2 or 3 opens a branch in six events, {{NEBULA_REBEL_CHASE}}, {{BROKEN_REBEL_DRONE}}, {{WRECKAGE_EVENT}} and {{TERRAFORMING_SCAN}} among them — and level 2 is the non-Slug way through the unlock chain.
Keeps the system half-alive under the hack in {{NEBULA_SLUG_MEDBAY}}, saves the dying survivor in {{NEBULA_BATTLEFIELD}} for a crew member, and cures the infected crewman in {{DONOR_PLAGUE}}.
Clean exits from {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}}, {{NEBULA_AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}} and {{AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM}}. Hiding from that Rebel patrol without it can instead lose you a jump to the fleet.
One crew member each turns a Slug trap around: the Mantis walks into {{SLUG_DISTRESS_TRICK}} expecting it, and the Rockman drinks whatever is in the flask at {{SLUG_DRINK}} on your behalf.

panels.title: Named things you can leave with

items.text: **Anti-Bio Beam** — the surrender offer at {{NEBULA_SLUG_FIGHT_UNLOCK}}. It is the same choice as the unlock chain, so you get one or the other.
A named Slug crew member from {{SLUG_DISTRESS_RESCUE}} — he asks 55 scrap, and sometimes waives it if you start powering up the FTL instead.
A Slug at {{SLUG_DISTRESS_QUESTION}}: the arrival text tells you how many moons the planet has, and that is the answer. Guessing costs scrap, fuel and drone parts.
An Engi at {{DONOR_PONY}}, a human at {{DONOR_PLAGUE}}, and a Mantis, Rockman or Engi at {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}}.
Two are guaranteed and both are {{NEBULA_STORE_SLUG}} — a Slug who teleports onto your bridge and lays his stock out on the helm. A conventional {{STORE}} may or may not be placed.
An unnamed weapon for 45 scrap from {{NEBULA_WEAPONS_TRADER}}, who may also take the scrap and hand over nothing. Mind Control gets him talking about what it actually is.

The hacker family is the real hazard: doors locked open next to fire weapons, oxygen cut, medbay dark with boarders already aboard, or shields, oxygen or weapons halved by your own answer at {{NEBULA_SLUG_CHOOSE_DEATH}}.
Six events put someone on your ship. {{NEBULA_SLUG_MEDBAY}} lands two Slugs while your medbay is off, and {{STORM_BOARDING}} drops three to four humans on you with no ship fight attached.
{{NEBULA_SLUG_HULLFIX}} patches your hull and then clamps you to the station: 15 fuel or 50 scrap. Refusing means a planted bomb, damage and a fight anyway.
Only three events in the pool can kill a crew member — {{SLUG_DISTRESS_TRICK}}, {{DONOR_PONY}} and {{DONOR_PLAGUE}}. This sector takes systems and scrap far more often than it takes people.

The empty entries can take up a lot of the map between them, and {{NEBULA_NOTHING_SLUG}} is the larger of the two. Every one of those is a jump spent for nothing, in a sector with only two guaranteed stores to restock at.
